summary: Built 1934 on Saddle Mountain, moved to Round Mountain (Kaibab NF) in 1960; Forest Service planned demolition in 2019-2020; Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone.

facts.design: 35’ Aermotor MC30 tower with 7’x7’ metal cab; a side door replaced the trap door
facts.status_note: Forest Service removal project listed as completed (decision signed 2020-03-05); Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone; no source describes the site now

access.note: National forest land; an undated travel account describes a spur road from FR 138 and a walk of about half a mile. No current access notice found

visit.trail_note: Undated travel account: spur road from FR 138 that the writer's truck, loaded with kayaks, could not manage, then about half a mile on foot. The site may hold no structure now; no source says so

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kaibab National Forest (Williams Ranger District)

events.note: Built on Saddle Mountain, Coconino NF, as a 35' Aermotor MC30 tower with 7'x7' metal cab
Moved to Round Mountain, Kaibab NF; side door replaced the trap door. A Coconino caption gives 1955-1960 for the move
Registered March 15, 2006 as US 664, AZ 59; nominated by Dave Lorenz
Forest Service scoping began December 17, 2019 on a proposal to demolish the Red Hill and Round Mountain towers
Decision signed March 5, 2020; project listed as completed; the page gives no date for the physical removal

corrections.why: NHLR says the tower was originally constructed on Saddle Mountain and moved to its current Kaibab NF location in 1960

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1960 for the move to Round Mountain; a Coconino NF caption says the base was allegedly moved between 1955 and 1960. The story uses the register's 1960 and says the sources differ.

NHLR names the Round Mountain tower an Aermotor MC30; the Coconino caption names the Saddle Mountain style MC-39. The caption may describe a different structure, so the story reports the register's model.
NHLR registered the tower in 2006; a 2018 Kaibab album shows it inactive; a Forest Service removal project is listed as completed in 2020; the Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone.

notes_for_editor: Status gone rests on the Fire Lookout Association list and a Forest Service removal project marked completed. No source says when or whether the tower was physically taken down, and none describes the site now. Staffing and access come from an undated album and an undated travel account, so they show only what those pages said when written. The Kaibab project documents on Pinyon Public were not read and may record the demolition. Search budget used: 2 searches; 6 page reads succeeded plus one 404 (Wikipedia has no Round Mountain article).
